units.text: Use when the goal is to move existing tests from the deprecated v1 Compose test APIs to the v2 APIs.
1. Run the tests and record the exact command and result as the baseline.

2. Find every use of the v1 APIs in [test-suite-structure.md](../core/test-suite-structure.md#api-mappings). Only the APIs that establish the test environment have been updated: [coroutines.md](../testing-patterns/coroutines.md#dispatchers-in-the-v1-and-v2-apis).

quotes.quote: Use the following table to map deprecated v1 APIs to their v2 replacements:
This update does not duplicate the entire API surface; only the APIs that establish the test environment have been updated

units.text: 3. Check the module's Compose UI test dependency versions. The v2 testing API changes are included in `androidx.compose.ui:ui-test-junit4:1.11.0-alpha03+` and `androidx.compose.ui:ui-test:1.11.0-alpha03+`: [flaky-tests.md](../debugging/flaky-tests.md#coroutine-timing-v1-vs-v2).

quotes.quote: The v2 testing API changes are included in androidx.compose.ui:ui-test-junit4:1.11.0-alpha03+ and androidx.compose.ui:ui-test:1.11.0-alpha03+.

units.text: 4. Find tests that depend on when a launched coroutine runs. The v1 APIs used `UnconfinedTestDispatcher`, which executed a launched coroutine immediately. The v2 APIs use `StandardTestDispatcher` by default for the running composition, which queues it until the test explicitly advances the virtual clock: [coroutines.md](../testing-patterns/coroutines.md#dispatchers-in-the-v1-and-v2-apis).

quotes.quote: v1 APIs (UnconfinedTestDispatcher)
When a coroutine was launched, it executed immediately on the current thread, often finishing before the next line of test code ran
v2 APIs (StandardTestDispatcher)
When a coroutine is launched, it is queued and does not execute until the test explicitly advances the virtual clock
While the v1 APIs relied on the UnconfinedTestDispatcher, the v2 APIs use the StandardTestDispatcher by default for the running composition

units.text: 5. Find tests that use Compose test APIs alongside the Kotlin `runTest` API: [flaky-tests.md](../debugging/flaky-tests.md#migrate-to-runcomposeuitest).

quotes.quote: If you're using Compose test APIs alongside the Kotlin runTest API, it's strongly recommended to switch to runComposeUiTest.

units.text: 6. Find calls of overloads that accept individual configuration parameters such as `effectContext`, `runTestContext`, or `testTimeout`. Several of these overloads are deprecated: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#deprecations).

quotes.quote: Within the overloads for creating setup functions in tests, several overloads that accept individual configuration parameters -- such as effectContext, runTestContext, or testTimeout -- are deprecated

units.text: 7. Find code that creates an instance of `AndroidComposeUiTestEnvironment` by its constructor or subclasses it. Its default test dispatcher switched from `UnconfinedTestDispatcher` to `StandardTestDispatcher`: [coroutines.md](../testing-patterns/coroutines.md#api-mappings).

quotes.quote: The default test dispatcher used for running composition in the AndroidComposeUiTestEnvironment class has switched from UnconfinedTestDispatcher to StandardTestDispatcher. This affects cases where you create an instance using the constructor, or subclass AndroidComposeUiTestEnvironment, and call that constructor.

units.text: 8. Find tests that rely on non-touch input modes configured through instrumentation APIs before the test starts. They can fail during migration: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#input-mode).

quotes.quote: Tests can fail during migration if they rely on non-touch input modes configured through instrumentation APIs before the test starts

units.text: - List each v1 use with its file and line and its replacement from the API mappings, and say which of the cases above apply to it.

- Most tests relying on standard Compose test APIs, such as `waitForIdle()`, should continue to work with no changes. Name the tests you expect to need changes and the reason: [flaky-tests.md](../debugging/flaky-tests.md#coroutine-timing-v1-vs-v2).

quotes.quote: Standard Compose test APIs (such as waitForIdle()) already handle this synchronization, so most tests relying on these standard APIs should continue to work with no changes

units.text: - Give the baseline command and result.
- Make one kind of change at a time, and run the tests after each.
- Update the package imports to the replacements in the mappings. You can generally use Find + Replace for this: [coroutines.md](../testing-patterns/coroutines.md#dispatchers-in-the-v1-and-v2-apis).

quotes.quote: When upgrading to v2 APIs, you can generally use Find + Replace to update the package imports and adopt the new dispatcher changes.

units.text: - If an assertion fails right after launching a task, use `waitForIdle` or `runOnIdle` to execute queued tasks before asserting: [flaky-tests.md](../debugging/flaky-tests.md#failures-after-upgrading-to-v2).

quotes.quote: Use waitForIdle) or runOnIdle) to execute queued tasks before asserting.
Using waitForIdle advances the clock until the UI is idle, verifying the coroutine has run.

units.text: - In scenarios involving manual synchronization, such as when auto-advancing is disabled, use `runCurrent()` to execute queued tasks without advancing the virtual clock: [flaky-tests.md](../debugging/flaky-tests.md#run-queued-coroutines-without-advancing-time).

quotes.quote: In scenarios involving manual synchronization, such as when auto-advancing is disabled, launching a coroutine does not result in immediate execution because the test clock is paused. To execute coroutines in the queue without advancing the virtual clock, use the
In contrast to waitForIdle(), which advances the test clock until the UI stabilizes, runCurrent() executes pending tasks while maintaining the current virtual time.

units.text: - For tests that use Compose test APIs alongside `runTest`, switch to `runComposeUiTest`: [flaky-tests.md](../debugging/flaky-tests.md#migrate-to-runcomposeuitest).

quotes.quote: If you're using Compose test APIs alongside the Kotlin runTest API, it's strongly recommended to switch to runComposeUiTest
Using createComposeRule in conjunction with runTest creates two separate clocks: one for Compose, and one for the test coroutine scope
This configuration can force you to manually synchronize the test scheduler
The runComposeUiTest API automatically executes your test block within its own runTest scope
The test clock is synchronized with the Compose environment, so you no longer need to manage the scheduler manually

The runComposeUiTest API automatically executes your test block within its own runTest scope. The test clock is synchronized with the Compose environment, so you no longer need to manage the scheduler manually.

units.text: - Replace the deprecated individual parameters with `ComposeUiTestConfig`: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#compose-test-environment).

quotes.quote: Within the overloads for creating setup functions in tests, several overloads that accept individual configuration parameters -- such as effectContext, runTestContext, or testTimeout -- are deprecated
Update your tests to use ComposeUiTestConfig instead

units.text: - Specify the required input mode in `ComposeUiTestConfig`, for a test class through the rule or for one test through `runComposeUiTest`: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#input-mode).

quotes.quote: To resolve this, specify the required input mode in ComposeUiTestConfig:
class FocusTest { @get:Rule val rule = createComposeRule( config = ComposeUiTestConfig(inputMode = InputMode.Keyboard) ) @Test fun testFocus() {} }
To configure the input mode for individual test cases instead of the entire test class, pass ComposeUiTestConfig to runComposeUiTest:

units.text: - While migrating, `AndroidComposeUiTestFlags.isInputModeSetForDeviceTests = false` temporarily retains the legacy input mode behavior. The flag will be removed in the future, so if only a small number of tests fail, it is recommended to change their configuration instead: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#deprecations).

quotes.quote: Alternatively, you can set AndroidComposeUiTestFlags.isInputModeSetForDeviceTests = false to temporarily disable setting the default input mode at the start of each test and retain legacy behavior while migrating your tests
This flag will be removed in the future, so if only a small number of tests fail, it is recommended to resolve the tests directly by changing their configuration instead

units.text: - Run the baseline commands again. Every test that passed before the change must still pass.

- Confirm the setup functions resolve to `androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.v2` for the rule functions and `androidx.compose.ui.test.v2` for the `run...` functions: [test-suite-structure.md](../core/test-suite-structure.md#api-mappings).

quotes.quote: androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.createComposeRule | androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.v2.createComposeRule
androidx.compose.ui.test.runComposeUiTest | androidx.compose.ui.test.v2.runComposeUiTest

units.text: - For each test that failed after the change, check whether it launches a task and its assertion fails immediately, because with the v2 APIs coroutines are queued rather than executed immediately, so the task never actually ran before the result was checked: [flaky-tests.md](../debugging/flaky-tests.md#failures-after-upgrading-to-v2).

quotes.quote: Cause: With the v2 APIs, coroutines are queued rather than executed immediately. The task was queued but never actually ran before the result was checked.
Failure: You launch a task (for example, a ViewModel loads data), but your assertion fails immediately because the data is still in a "Loading" state.

units.text: - When a migrated test newly fails, check whether v1 immediate execution had inadvertently masked a real timing issue or race condition that would occur in a live application, and report it as such if so: [coroutines.md](../testing-patterns/coroutines.md#dispatchers-in-the-v1-and-v2-apis).

quotes.quote: Unlike production behavior, this immediate execution could inadvertently mask real timing issues or race conditions that would occur in a live application

units.text: - For each changed test, break the behavior it checks, confirm the failure, then restore it.
- Re-read every statement against its reference file or official page.
- Delegate the survey by module: each read-only subagent lists the old setup functions and patterns in its module, with file and line.
- Keep for yourself: the edits, one file at a time, running that file's tests after each.
- After verification, delegate the challenge to a fresh reviewer: compare the migrated files with the migration reference and the baseline results.
- Migrate one file at a time, in the order the design lists.
- Remove temporary code added during the migration.
